headline: Lost-wallet task with three debit cards is clean: every gold write follows from the customer script, the tier table, and the card-closure rules.
solution_check: Reconstructed independently: verify, list accounts, read debit cards for the three accounts (needed to get card ids), freeze all three, read transactions (Light Green chk_mc78a5b9d2_3 has two status 'pending' rows, so its card stays frozen), count Light Blue replacements (dbc_mc78a5b9d2_lb issued 07/25/2025 'lost' and lb_old1 issued 03/15/2025 'lost', both inside 12 months, so a third is over the ENTRY limit and the customer declines the $25 fee), unfreeze then close Light Blue and Green as 'lost' (close_debit_card_4721 rejects FROZEN cards), and order Green EXPEDITED $15 CLASSIC $0. Replaying that sequence in a different order with float fees and an extra failed close on a frozen card matched the gold under both the verified and exact comparison.
prior_note: Prior review rated this clean; the v1.0.1 change only added the get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 read, which any agent needs to find the account ids, so the verdict stands.
notes: Unfreeze-before-close is forced by the tool and documented: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025 requirement 3 "The debit card must currently be in ACTIVE or PENDING status"; close_debit_card_4721 returns "cannot be closed. Current status: FROZEN". The failed close is a status rejection, so it logs close_debit_card_4721, which the gold logs anyway. Keeping the Light Blue card frozen instead of closing it fails (debit_cards differs), but the customer explicitly asks to close all three after confirming the wallet is gone, so closing is the reading the script supports. get_credit_card_accounts_by_user returns no records (doc_030 check is a no-op). Shipping address in the order is the on-file address string verbatim; the script never states a different address.
